newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Acacia says rain affects gold output.
newsitem.headline: Acacia says rain affects gold output.

text.p: Acacia Resources Ltd said on Wednesday gold output in the March quarter was affected by heavy rains at its mines in the Northern Territory, but was partly offset by higher production from the one-third owned Boddington mine in Western Australia.
Total production fell to 66,408 ounces, 10 percent below the record output of 73,920 ounces in the December quarter. Acacia did not release year-ago data for wholly-owned operations.
Acacia's equity production from Boddington rose to 30,476 ounces in the latest quarter, 13 percent above the December quarter and 15 percent above the year ago level.
The company's partners in Boddington are Normandy Mining Ltd with a 44.44 percent stake and Newcrest Mining Ltd with a 22.22 percent holding.
It said a full feasibility study had begun for the Wandoo extension at Boddington based on an estimated resource of 8.7 million ounces of gold and some copper.
The capital outlay was estmated at about A$260 million and initial annual gold output of 300,000 ounces.
The partners would consider recommendations for Wandoo before the end of 1997, with plant commissioning seen in mid-1999, Acacia said.
Drilling had indicated further major extensions at Wandoo with intersections including 149.3 metres at 1.90 g/t gold and 0.69 percent copper from 291 metres.

Acacia said gold production from its wholly-owned operations in the Northern Territory, Union Reefs and Brocks Creek, fell by 26 percent and 19 percent respectively compared with the December quarter.
Union Reefs output was 15,365 ounces while Brocks Creek achieved 10,768 ounces.
Equity production from the 40 percent-owned Tanami mine was 9,106 ounces. Acacia did not release comparative data.
The company said it expected to meet its forecast of producing more than 350,000 ounces of gold in calendar 1997 due to the start-up of the Sunrise Dam mine in the Northern Territory.
The first gold was poured at Sunrise on March 29, with 692 ounces poured in the month.
